2027-04-22.title: Thursday of the Fourth Week of Easter
readings: Of this man's posterity God has brought to Israel a Savior, Jesus, as he promised
For ever I will sing the goodness of the Lord (or: Alleluia)
Whoever receives one whom I send receives me
2027-04-22.alt: Easter weekday. The paschal candle burns beside the ambo; the Alleluia returns in the antiphons and the Gospel acclamation; the Regina Caeli (Queen of Heaven) replaces the Angelus until Pentecost. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-04-22.verse: Very truly, I tell you, whoever receives one whom I send receives me; and whoever receives me receives him who sent me.
theo: Paul and his companions sail from Cyprus to the mainland of Asia Minor, and Luke slips in a small, painful detail: “John, however, left them and returned to Jerusalem.” Young John Mark turned back. We are not told why: fear of the hard road over the Taurus mountains, homesickness, or disagreement. Later this desertion would cause a sharp quarrel between Paul and Barnabas (Acts 15:37–39). But the story does not end there. Years afterwards Paul would write from prison: “Get Mark and bring him with you, for he is useful in my ministry” (2 Timothy 4:11). And the Church remembers this same Mark as the writer of the Gospel that bears his name. The one who turned back was given a second chance, and he became a pillar. God does not throw away those who fail.

At Antioch in Pisidia, high on the plateau, Paul and Barnabas go to the synagogue on the sabbath. After the reading of the Law and the Prophets the officials invite them to speak: “Brothers, if you have any word of exhortation for the people, give it.” Paul stands up and begins with deep respect: “You Israelites, and others who fear God, listen.” His sermon is a loving retelling of Israel's history: God “chose our ancestors,” brought them out of Egypt “with uplifted arm,” “put up with them in the wilderness” for forty years, gave them the land, the judges, and the kings. Then David, “a man after my heart, who will carry out all my wishes.” And from David's line, as God promised, comes the Savior, Jesus. Paul's first preaching is not a rejection of Israel's story but a proclamation of its fulfilment. The Psalm sings the same faithfulness: “I will sing of your steadfast love, O Lord, forever,” and recalls God's oath to David: “I have found my servant David; with my holy oil I have anointed him.”

Paul ends this part of his speech with John the Baptist, who said: “I am not worthy to untie the thong of the sandals on his feet.” The greatest of the prophets knew he was only a servant. The Gospel takes us back to the Last Supper, just after Jesus has knelt and washed the feet of his disciples. He says: “Very truly, I tell you, servants are not greater than their master, nor are messengers greater than the one who sent them.” If the Lord washed feet, his apostles must do the same. “If you know these things, you are blessed if you do them.” Even the shadow of betrayal is present: Jesus quotes the Psalm, “The one who ate my bread has lifted his heel against me,” so that when it happens the disciples may not lose faith but believe that “I am he.” And then a promise that gives the humblest messenger great dignity: “whoever receives one whom I send receives me; and whoever receives me receives him who sent me.” The servant is small, but the One who sends him is God.
conn: A city near the southern coast of present-day Turkey. From there the road climbed steeply over the Taurus mountains to Antioch in Pisidia, about 1,100 metres above sea level.
Not Antioch in Syria but a Roman colony in the interior of Asia Minor, near modern Yalvaç. Luke records Paul's sermon there as a model of his preaching to Jews.
Readings from the Law (Torah) and the Prophets, followed by an exhortation. The pattern of reading and preaching passed into the Christian Liturgy of the Word.
Gentiles who worshipped the God of Israel and attended the synagogue without becoming Jews. Cornelius was one of them (Acts 10:2).
Paul combines 1 Samuel 13:14, Psalm 89:20 and Isaiah 44:28. David's faults were great, but his heart turned back to God; the Messiah would come from his line (2 Samuel 7:12–16).
The task of a slave. Rabbinic teaching said a disciple might do every service for his master except this one. John the Baptist says he is unworthy even of that (Luke 3:16).
Psalm 41:9, the lament of one betrayed by a table companion. To lift the heel against someone was a gesture of contempt.
In Greek egō eimi, “I am,” echoing the divine name revealed to Moses (Exodus 3:14). Jesus speaks it as the one who knows the future and holds it.
altar: Jesus said these words at the table of the Last Supper, after washing his disciples' feet. Every Mass holds together the Eucharist and service: the Lord who gives himself in the Bread is the Lord who kneels to wash feet.
The Liturgy of the Word follows the pattern Paul knew in the synagogue: the Scriptures are read, and then the word is explained for the people. The Church received this treasure from Israel.
outline: Ask: have I ever turned back from something God asked of me?
Point 1 · The one who turned back
John Mark leaves, and is later restored.
Paul retells Israel's story and proclaims its fulfilment.
Not greater than the master; received as the master.
A basin, a towel, and a pair of dusty sandals by the door.
“Whoever receives one whom I send receives me.”
live: Think of someone who let you down. Like Paul with Mark, find one way to show that the door is not closed.
At the family prayer tonight, let each person name one time God was faithful to your family.
Choose one hidden service at home or in the parish this week, the kind no one thanks you for, and do it for Jesus.
Welcome the priest, the catechist or the house-visiting Vincentian as you would welcome Christ.
fathers: Paul does not begin by rebuking his hearers. He begins with the story they love, the kindness of God to their fathers, and so leads them gently to Christ, who is the fulfilment of the promises.
John the Baptist was so great that he could have been taken for the Christ; yet he humbled himself and said he was not worthy to loose his sandal. The more he lowered himself, the higher he stood.
The sharpness of Paul and the gentleness of Barnabas both served Mark: the one corrected him, the other encouraged him, and so he who had turned back became useful. Let no one despair after a fall.
magis: Jesus is the One sent by the Father; he sends the apostles as the Father sent him, so that whoever receives them receives him.
St John the Baptist, the Lord's precursor, the voice who prepares his way.
Humility is the foundation of prayer.
The Liturgy of the Word inherited from the synagogue; the Church's bond with Israel in the liturgy.
The Old Testament as true word of God, and the unity of the two Testaments.
saints: Cousin of Barnabas, companion of Paul and Peter, identified by tradition with St Mark the Evangelist. He turned back at Perga but later became Paul's valued helper. His feast (25 April) is not kept this year because it falls on the Fifth Sunday of Easter.
23 Apr: St George; St Adalbert. 24 Apr: St Fidelis of Sigmaringen. 25 Apr: Fifth Sunday of Easter.
2027-04-22.prayer: Lord Jesus, Servant and Master, you knelt to wash the feet of your disciples and you sent them out as the Father sent you. Make us humble servants, glad to do the lowly tasks of love. Thank you for your faithfulness through all generations, from Abraham and David to this very day. When we turn back like John Mark, call us again and make us useful in your service. Teach us to receive in your messengers your own presence, and in you the Father who sent you. You live and reign for ever and ever. Alleluia. Amen.

quick: John Mark turned back, but later Paul called him useful: God gives second chances.
Paul preached in the synagogue God's faithfulness to Israel, fulfilled in Jesus, son of David.
Jesus: servants are not greater than their master; whoever receives my messenger receives me.
2027-04-22.action: Do one hidden act of service today that no one will thank you for.
2027-04-22.question: Is there someone I have refused to give a second chance?
catechism: The apostles, sent as Christ was sent.
John the Baptist, precursor of the Lord.
kidsaint: John the Baptist was a great prophet. Huge crowds came to hear him by the river Jordan. Some people even thought he was the Messiah. But John said: I am not even good enough to untie his sandals! He pointed everyone to Jesus. Lesson: being humble means we point to Jesus, not to ourselves.
2027-04-22.special: Easter weekday: Regina Caeli at noon; Alleluia in the antiphons.
term: From the Greek for “gathering.” The Jewish house of prayer and study, where the Law and Prophets were read every sabbath. The Christian Liturgy of the Word grew from this tradition of reading and explaining the Scriptures.

family.explain: At the Last Supper Jesus, the Lord and Teacher, knelt down and washed his friends' feet. Then he said: a servant is not greater than his master. If I have washed your feet, you should wash one another's feet. You will be happy if you do it.
family.intention: We pray for all who serve others quietly: mothers and fathers, nurses, cleaners, and all who work without thanks.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one ‘foot-washing job’ each of us can do for the family this week?” Choose one and do it without being asked.

illus: A young man from Alappuzha left the seminary in his second year, ashamed and confused. For a long time he avoided the priests who had taught him. Years later, married and working as a teacher, he received a phone call from the old rector: our parish youth have no one to guide them; you were always good with young people. Will you help? He hesitated, then said yes. Today he leads the diocesan youth movement. He says: I thought my turning back was the end of my story. God thought it was a chapter.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you washed the feet of your disciples. Make us humble servants and faithful messengers. Alleluia. Amen.
share: John, however, left them and returned to Jerusalem (Acts 13:13). Where have I turned back, and how is God calling me again?
Of this man's posterity God has brought to Israel a Savior, Jesus, as he promised (Acts 13:23). How has God kept his promises in my life?
Servants are not greater than their master (John 13:16). What humble service is Jesus asking of me?
pm.resp: For ever I will sing the goodness of the Lord.
interc: For all who have turned back from their vocation or their faith, that God may give them a second chance.
For our Jewish brothers and sisters, heirs of the promises to Abraham and David.
For priests and all who serve in the Church, that they may be humble servants like their Master.
For those who serve without recognition, that the Lord may reward them.
For our group, that we may receive every messenger of Christ with faith.
pm.close: Father, you are faithful to every generation. Make us humble servants of your Son and messengers of his love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, in today's first reading there is one small, sad sentence: John, however, left them and returned to Jerusalem (Acts 13:13). John Mark turned back from the mission. Perhaps he was afraid. Perhaps he was homesick. We do not know.

But we know the end of the story. Years later, Paul, who had been angry with him, wrote: get Mark and bring him with you, for he is useful in my ministry (2 Timothy 4:11). And the Church remembers him as St Mark, the writer of a Gospel. God does not throw away those who fail. If you have turned back from something, he is calling you again.

Then Paul preaches in the synagogue. He begins with respect: you Israelites, and others who fear God, listen. He tells the story of God's faithfulness: Egypt, the desert, the land, the judges, King David. And from David's family, God has brought a Savior, Jesus, as he promised. Our God keeps his promises.
Paul remembers John the Baptist, who said: I am not worthy to untie the thong of the sandals on his feet (Acts 13:25). The greatest prophet knew he was a servant.

In the Gospel Jesus has just washed the feet of his disciples. He says: servants are not greater than their master (John 13:16). If the Lord kneels, we must kneel too. And he gives his messengers a great dignity: whoever receives one whom I send receives me.
Let us ask today for humble hearts, ready to serve, and for the grace never to give up on anyone, not even on ourselves. Alleluia. Amen.
kids: Children, John Mark got scared and went home in the middle of a journey with Paul. But later he came back, and he even wrote one of the four Gospels!
If we make a mistake, Jesus gives us another chance. Let us say: Jesus, help me to try again!

intro: Theme: “Whoever receives one whom I send receives me.”
The one who turned back and was restored, God's faithfulness to Israel, and the dignity of humble service.

sub: David, a man after God's heart.
q: I will sing of your steadfast love, O Lord, forever; with my mouth I will proclaim your faithfulness to all generations.
Of this man's posterity God has brought to Israel a Savior, Jesus, as he promised;
points.apply: Write down three promises God has kept in your life and thank him for them tonight.

points.h: Not worthy to untie his sandals
sub: John the Baptist points away from himself.
q: He has told you, O mortal, what is good; and what does the Lord require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?
Very truly, I tell you, servants are not greater than their master, nor are messengers greater than the one who sent them.
points.apply: Do one lowly task this week that you usually leave to others.

q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace,
Very truly, I tell you, whoever receives one whom I send receives me; and whoever receives me receives him who sent me.
points.apply: Welcome the next priest, catechist or Church visitor to your home as Christ himself.

concl: God keeps faith with Israel and fulfils his promises in Jesus, son of David.
He gives second chances to those who turn back, and he is present in his humble messengers.
2027-04-22.resolve: Give someone a second chance this week, as Paul did with Mark.
